exterior:
Use case: stylized-concept. Create a large landscape ORTHOGRAPHIC ARCHITECTURAL TURNAROUND sheet for BLUEBIRD DINER based on the attached user's image. This attached image is the ONLY visual/style reference; ignore all previous Bluebird designs and renders. Match its oil-painted realism EXACTLY in palette, painterly handling, quiet broad values, weathered pale timber above dark faded teal lower siding, grey umber exposed wood, muted rusty metal awning, soft northern coastal daylight and amber window interiors. Not a generic Victorian building, NOT a clean game miniature, NOT a boxy full-height two-storey block.
User-required architectural adaptation: a BROAD LOW ground-floor CORNER DINER with a MUCH SMALLER SECOND FLOOR set back toward the REAR LEFT. Ground-floor footprint 12 m wide by 10 m deep; upper dwelling footprint 6 m by 6 m occupying the rear-left quarter-to-third, set back 4 m from the front and 6 m from the right street face. Ground-floor roof height around 3.4 m; total upper roof height around 6.3 m. It must unmistakably read as a generous one-storey diner with a modest set-back upstairs dwelling, NOT two equal stacked floors. Flat/shallow pitched weathered roof profiles, restrained cornice, and the corner sign massing of the reference. The two street faces are the FRONT and the RIGHT. A chamfered glazed corner entrance joins these two faces, with a big warm corner display window, bench, short awning, downpipes and pavement edge following the reference. Sign text changed ONLY to "BLUEBIRD DINER"; keep a small vertical "EATS" sign if space allows. No people, no new story clues, no exterior back door.
Arrange exactly THREE LARGE elevations in a single row at the SAME SCALE and ground datum: "FRONT" on left, "RIGHT SIDE" middle, "REAR" on right. Each is a true straight-on orthographic view: no perspective, no isometric view. Keep all roof/floor heights consistent between views. The small upper volume should appear at the LEFT of the front elevation, at the BACK (right on page) of the right side elevation, and at the RIGHT of the rear elevation due to reverse viewing direction. The lower floor extends visibly beyond the upstairs. Show the corner entrance at the front's right end and side's front end, without making two independent entrances. Windows: dining windows along front and street side, kitchen service windows at rear, modest upper living/bedroom windows. Make the same openings correspond logically across elevations. Rear wall has windows only, no door.
Clean bone-white drawing-paper sheet with fine structural outlines enriched by the exact painterly surface treatment of the attached reference. Clear wall/roof silhouettes, readable aperture recesses and material changes; broad tonal masses and irregular dry brush, no repeated dense grain or uniform black outlines. Neutral material-reading lighting; no shadows covering half the elevations. Thin horizontal ground/upper-floor/eaves guide lines, and a small 4-swatch material strip along the bottom.
Text limited to "BLUEBIRD / CORNER DINER", "FRONT", "RIGHT SIDE", "REAR", "LARGE GROUND FLOOR / SMALL SET-BACK UPPER FLOOR", "DESIGN REFERENCE" and the actual signs. Do not add fake dimensions, paragraphs, fantasy props, surrounding town scenery, or any human figure. The image must be usable as front/side/rear Blender modeling reference while retaining the exact oil-painted visual identity of the supplied image.

Image 1 is the user's authoritative oil-painting STYLE AND BUILDING CHARACTER reference. Image 2 is the new EXTERIOR TURNAROUND: preserve its broad low ground floor, much smaller rear-left upper dwelling, faded ivory weatherboards, teal lower wall, low roof and single glazed corner entrance. No old equal-size two-storey block.
Sheet layout on bone-white paper: top LEFT is a true straight-down ground-floor plan, top RIGHT is a true straight-down upper-floor plan AT THE SAME SCALE with the whole lower footprint lightly outlined beneath it; bottom is a large LONGITUDINAL CUT SECTION A-A THROUGH THE STAIR, showing the continuous climb, floor opening, supporting walls/posts/beams and roof levels. Strict orthographic plans/section, no perspective dollhouse. Use fine construction linework plus restrained authentic oil-painted material fields; exact same mature painterly material palette as references, not a clean CAD neon diagram.
Design geometry (these are authoring design assumptions, not surveyed measurements): lower floor rectangle 12m wide x10m deep, with a 1.3m chamfer at FRONT-RIGHT corner. FRONT/street is at the BOTTOM of both plans, REAR at the TOP, RIGHT STREET at the RIGHT. Upper dwelling x=0..6m, depth y=4..10m, i.e. rear LEFT 6x6m footprint, front setback 4m and right setback 6m. Thus about 30% upper-floor coverage. Remaining lower roof is UNWALKABLE ROOF, no terrace access or outdoor stairs. Lower floor level 0, upper floor +3.2m, upper ceiling +5.8m, shallow roof around +6.2m.
GROUND FLOOR: front zone y=0..6m is dining; rear strip y=6..10m is working kitchen. One single glazed chamfered entry at front-right opens to dining. Front dining storefront on bottom wall, two street-side windows on right wall; rear kitchen windows on top wall, NO exterior back door. Three green leather booths along the front-left window zone, maple lunch counter with six red stools toward right side running front-to-back, clear entry and service aisles. Behind counter, spring double doors at x=7..8.4m in y=6m dividing wall connect kitchen; adjacent serving hatch. Kitchen range, oven and iron stew pot on left, steel prep table center-left, triple sink on back wall, pantry and refrigerator back-right. Straight steep indoor stair on x=4.8..5.9m, running from bottom landing near rear y=9.7m UP toward front y=5.7m, entirely beneath the upper dwelling. Mark stair UP arrow and matching rectangular floor opening above. Preserve a clear kitchen route to bottom landing.
UPPER FLOOR: show ONLY the 6x6 rear-left dwelling inside a faint outline of the larger lower roof. Small bedroom at rear-left with iron bed and wardrobe; living area toward front/right with round cloth-covered table, dresser and rocking chair near the front-facing upstairs window. Stair landing connects living area to the same stair from kitchen, with handrail around the opening. Internal bedroom door, no new exterior upper door. Indicate simple loadbearing perimeter, dividing wall and a supporting beam below the front upper wall so it does not float over the dining room.
SECTION: clearly show larger low diner extending toward front beyond smaller upper dwelling at rear; full stair from kitchen floor through upper opening to landing; no stair ending against a slab, no floating upper walls. Cut structural components hatched, fixtures lightly drawn. Small callout showing roof, upper wall, upper floor, lower wall as separate future modeling assemblies is welcome if uncluttered.
Text limited to "BLUEBIRD / INTERIOR STRUCTURE", "GROUND FLOOR", "UPPER FLOOR", "SECTION A-A", "DINING", "KITCHEN", "LIVING", "BEDROOM", "UP", "FRONT STREET", "RIGHT STREET", "ROOF ONLY", "DESIGN ASSUMPTIONS: 12 x 10 m / UPPER 6 x 6 m". No tiny illegible paragraphs, no fake puzzle text, no people, no human silhouettes. Prioritize matched geometry, doors and stair relationships, NOT decorative extra furniture.
